title: ‘The Hunting Wives’ Season 2 Trailer Has Sapphic Sex and Sad Exes
content:
Season one of The Hunting Wives was a wild ride, and I have a feeling season two is going to be even wilder. The full trailer dropped and it has me clapping and kicking my feet at the sapphic chaos about to descend upon us.

The trailer opens with Sophie’s husband asking if Sophie is “still dreaming about her” (“her” being Margo) and a few flashing scenes implies that yes, yes she is.

Other things we see flash by: a glam cowgirl photo shoot, Margo being manipulative to all kinds of people, and Callie being a sad ex and using a photo of Margo as target practice.

This show also knows exactly what it is and is leaning into it. For example, the song playing is Nancy Sinatra’s “Bang Bang”, which is the perfect backdrop for this trailer full of guns and sex and chaos. And the tagline for the season is “someone is going down,” which the narrator says while the visuals cut between a dead body and also a more…explicit interpretation of the phrase.

Based on how season one ended, I can’t wait to find out how Sophie ends up back in Margo’s bed (and her bubble bath!), and luckily we only have one month left to wait.

title: ‘Grey’s Anatomy’ Kicked Off Season 23 With a Sapphic Smooch
content:
Grey’s Anatomy came back with a bang. (Well, a smooch. But we’ll get there.) Amelia spent the entire episode getting the cold shoulder from Toni because, as I’m sure you remember, we left them last season with Toni showing up at Amelia’s door to profess her love for her, only to realize a naked Cass was already in Amelia’s apartment.

When we return for season 23(!), Toni is giving Amelia the cold shoulder all day. Amelia desperately wants to talk to her, but Toni isn’t hearing her out. They clash over work decisions, and Amelia starts to get frustrated. And at this point I was afraid the show was ending their storyline. I thought it was going to be a dramatic fight and then back to no wlw relationships on the show. I was thankfully wrong!

Eventually, the day leads Amelia to Toni’s front door, where she apologizes again for sleeping with Cass, and explains it was an emotional reaction to being so sure Toni was about get back together with her ex. She regrets it if it means she would lose Toni. She says she’s truly, madly, deeply in love with Toni and that if Toni is done, she’ll move on, but if not, she really doesn’t want to let what they have died. Toni considers her for a moment but then breaks; she’s still in love with Amelia, and she’s not done. author: Valerie Anne
title: ‘The Body’ Is a Sapphic, Ritual-Gone-Wrong Teen Horror Show Coming to Netflix
content:
Do you ever feel like a show was made just for you using all your favorite media keywords? That’s how I felt when I first heard about Netflix’s The Body. I saw Catholic school, dancers, ritual-gone-wrong, horror and I was beyond sold.

And in case those words and phrases didn’t make it obvious: The story is also sapphic. Writer and creator Quinn Shephard (who acted in movies like The Miseducation of Cameron Post and wrote/directed episodes of Under the Bridge) started writing the show the year she came out. She says: “It’s satirizing some of the trauma of growing up queer and repressed and the confusion around that.”

A lot of the main cast of girls are relative newcomers on the scene (aka they don’t have Wikipedia “personal life” pages yet) so I’m not sure who among them are queer, but the show WILL feature lesbian reality star Gabby Windey in a recurring role as a coach. Also, almost all of the episodes have women listed as writers.

The show looks freaky and weird in all the best ways, and I can’t wait. I hope it’s just as fun as shows like Yellowjackets and even Mike Flanagan’s Carrie. May the teens-getting-into-supernatural-mischief genre never die.

The series drops next month and you can watch the full official trailer right now!

title: Horror Comedy ‘The Blood Countess’ Imagines Elizabeth Báthory as a Lesbian Vampire
content:
If I had a nickel for every piece of queer media about 17th century Hungarian countess Elizabeth Báthory released this year, I’d have two nickels. Which isn’t a lot, but it’s weird that it happened twice. After her strange appearance in Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story, she also appears in the vampire horror comedy The Blood Countess directed and co-written by lesbian filmmaker Ulrike Ottinger. In the film, Báthory (played by Isabelle Huppert) wakes from a long slumber and finds herself in modern-day Vienna, searching for a book that could cure her vampirism.

I find two things interesting about the fact that the countess has appeared in two queer adaptations this year. The first is that Lizzie Borden actually never really portrayed her as a lesbian, even though she was set up parallel to Lizzie and lesbian serial killer Aileen Wuornos and was played by the same actress who played Lizzie’s lover. Before the much-later rumors that Elizabeth Báthory bathed in the blood of virgin girls, the crimes she was accused of were more along the lines of torture and cannibalism. So it’s interesting that was then interpreted as lesbianism. Then again, she was luring young women to her castle with three of her closest gal pals, so, who knows I guess.
